# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- **Name:** ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- **Version:** v1.0
- **Intended use:** Screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- **Clinic:** FR-MES-01 (Messidor-2, France)
- **Period:** Week 1 (starting 2026-01-05)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift identified that retinal scans from Clinic FR-MES-01 no longer match the image parameters on which the AI model was validated (drift score 0.99, where 0.5 indicates baseline training data and 1 indicates a clear difference).

Because expert clinical grades for the 50 scans taken this week are not yet available, the catch rate (sensitivity for referable disease) cannot be verified. The AI model is currently referring patients at a higher rate than usual: 80% of scans this week, compared with 68% in the training dataset.

## 4. Potential patient impact
Because the catch rate cannot be verified, potential missed cases cannot be estimated. No patient harm has been confirmed.

## 5. Likely cause
Significant changes in camera hardware and image quality metrics (reduced sharpness, contrast, and overall quality, alongside increased image resolution) at Clinic FR-MES-01 compared to the training set. (Category: camera or image quality; confidence: 85%; source: gemini)

Evidence:
- Drift alarm triggered with a drift score of 0.99 (0.5 = like training, 1 = clearly different) across 50 scans.
- Mean image quality decreased from 0.5 in training to 0.198 (-0.604 relative change).
- Mean sharpness decreased from 0.000399 to 0.000213 (-0.467 relative change).
- Mean contrast decreased from 0.0963 to 0.0564 (-0.414 relative change).
- Mean brightness decreased from 0.373 to 0.328 (-0.119 relative change).
- Mean resolution increased from 1020.0 px to 2010.0 px (0.967 relative change).
- Referral rate increased from 0.685 to 0.8 (0.169 relative change) and mean referral score increased from 0.193 to 0.269 (0.395 relative change).
- Evidence from referral rate changes is weak due to the small sample size of 50 scans.

## 6. Action
ClinicDrift paused the AI system at this clinic because the scans drifted beyond the model's validated range, meaning the catch rate cannot be verified. It is recommended that scans from this clinic are sent for manual human grading until the following checks are complete.

Checks:
- [ ] Verify camera model, lens condition, and lighting/focus settings at Clinic FR-MES-01.
- [ ] Inspect image acquisition pipeline and pre-processing handling for 2010.0 px resolution scans.
- [ ] Audit patient acquisition protocol and operator training regarding glare and image sharpness.
- [ ] Conduct clinical re-evaluation of flagged images to confirm whether true pathology or image artefacts influenced the referral score.

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): This alarm is part of ongoing monitoring of the device in use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): Any model change made in response should fall within an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: See recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
